note: Wikidata q-ids only, searched in Czech and confirmed against the Czech description so that the item names Prague and not one of the seven other Czech towns with a Staroměstské náměstí. Converted from the Explorer product: all ten of its spots carry over and seven places are added, two of them museums with an interior, because the Explorer gives none. The Explorer's own lat/lng were hand-written and are not used anywhere — that is what this pipeline replaces. NO ENTRANCE IS CLAIMED: no door in Prague has been measured, so every point is the centroid, area or viewpoint it actually is. TWO INSTITUTION-VERSUS-BUILDING TRAPS, both caught here: 'Národní muzeum' (Q188112) is the institution, five research institutes and thirteen million objects across a dozen addresses, so its coordinate is not a door — Q43755714 is the neo-Renaissance building of 1891 at the top of Wenceslas Square that a child actually walks into. Likewise 'Národní technické muzeum' (Q96482839) is an organisation; Q1789383 is Milan Babuška's building on Letná. CENTRE: this is Wikidata's point for Malá Strana (Q753289), NOT Wikidata's point for Prague itself (Q1085). The city's own coordinate is 50.0875, 14.421389 — character for character the coordinate of Staroměstské náměstí (Q421678) — so using it makes the audit report the Old Town Square as sitting 0 m from the city centre. That would be a false positive on the reference point, not a fault in the place: the square has a perfectly good coordinate of its own and is exactly where it should be. The two other obvious substitutes are both inside the 60 m centroid check as well — Staré Město (Q748211) lands 41 m from Havelské tržiště and Praha 1 (Q973974) lands 59 m from Charles Bridge — while Malá Strana's point is 298 m clear of the nearest place and still sits between the castle hill and the river.

places.name: Staroměstský orloj
places.note: The clock, not the town hall it is bolted to. Q729370 is the machine and its two dials, which is the thing a child stands in front of; Staroměstská radnice is a separate item and a separate building with its own tower and its own door.

places.name: Lennonova zeď
places.note: Q1630131 is the wall itself ('zeď v Praze na Malé Straně'). Q107161512 is a separate item for the memorial and was not used.

places.name: Historická budova Národního muzea
places.note: The BUILDING, not the institution. Q188112 is the National Museum as an organisation and its point would be an administrative fiction; Q43755714 is Josef Schulz's 1891 palace on Wenceslas Square. Added to the Explorer's ten: the Explorer walks past this building twice and never goes in, and the city needs two museums with a real interior.

places.name: Budova Národního technického muzea
places.note: The BUILDING again. Q96482839 is the organisation. Q1789383 is Milan Babuška's 1938–1941 building on Letná, whose transport hall is the room this city is worth visiting for. Added; the Explorer has no museum at all.

places.name: Vyšehrad
places.note: Q616334 is the fortress. Q21891843 is the city district of the same name and Q2013931 is the metro station; neither is the place. Added.

places.name: Staronová synagoga
places.note: Added. Q102065754 shares the name but is an archive holding, not a building.

places.name: Havelské tržiště
places.note: Added, for the food category. No Wikipedia article in any language, so this one will grade C on Wikidata alone unless Overpass answers; that is a thin audit trail, not a disagreement.
